result.title: Riding the Fixed-Point Curve: Image Classification in the Continuous Thought Machine
result.comment: 19 pages, 8 figures, 4 tables. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Symmetry and Geometry in Neural Representations (NeurReps), extended abstract track (non-archival)
result.summary: The Continuous Thought Machine (CTM) is a recurrent network that attends to inputs and makes predictions based on the synchronization between its neurons. On tasks spanning many domains, it displays emergent thought processes that have not been explained. We report a number of findings about how the CTM classifies images, focusing on ImageNet. Each thinking step is an attracting but strongly non-normal map exhibiting balanced amplification (Murphy and Miller, 2009); while attraction is already present at CTM initialization, training highly promotes non-normality. By Banach's theorem, the neural state has a locally unique attracting fixed point, which moves at every step, and the thought trajectory is the curve these fixed points trace, followed one tick behind. Most of that curve's motion is shared across images, and visible as a previously reported traveling wave of activity across neurons. The attention schedule along the thought is largely generic: shuffling queries across images at every tick costs only 7 percent of classification accuracy, while image-independent increments predict the next query with R^2 = 0.98 (held out). Our results suggest that the CTM has found a single strategy to process all ImageNet images.

AI.brief_summary: 论文以 ImageNet 为例分析 Continuous Thought Machine（CTM）这类循环网络如何分类图像，刻画每个思考步骤的神经状态动力学：每步是吸引但强非正规的映射并伴随平衡放大，存在随步移动的局部唯一吸引不动点，思考轨迹即这些不动点勾勒的曲线，而该曲线大部分运动跨图像共享，注意力调度也近乎通用（打乱各图查询仅损失约 7% 精度）。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及 LVR 关注的循环 latent 状态是否真正承载图像证据：若思考轨迹与查询调度在不同图像间高度一致，可能提示 latent 状态的信息坍缩或泛化策略单一，可供核查 latent 内容使用、动态计算与停止决策的收益来源。
